name: Cashout
tagline: The tip log in Publication 531, sealed before she sleeps, with a second witness on every tip-out.
old_product: The paper tip log, the notes-app tally and the mileage notebook kept by tipped and gig workers
fresh_spin: At her usual close time a ten-second keypad logs cash, tip-out and Venmo, and the night is sealed with a timestamp so later corrections show as amendments.
boring_but: Boring on the surface, it's the tip log in Publication 531. But every night is sealed before she sleeps, and every tip-out has a second witness.
borrows_from: Afterlist (fresh spin 05): evidence tiers on every line (sealed same night > photo > reconstructed later)
#36 Settlement: seal the record at the time, before anyone knows it will matter
Ran It (fresh spin 01): the event (close of shift) prompts the record, not memory
summary: Cashout is a $39.99-a-year sealed tip log for workers paid in cash and Venmo: bartenders, servers, booth-renting stylists and valets. A notification at her usual close time opens a keypad for cash, tip-out and Venmo; the entry is sealed with a timestamp and corrections appear as visible amendments. A tip-out can be shared as an amount-free link from her own Messages, and once the co-worker accepts, each entry confirms the other. On the 1st she gets a Form 4070-style PDF to hand to her employer herself, and in January an evidence-tiered ledger for her preparer; Rebuild 2026 ($29, credited) reconstructs earlier months from Venmo, Cash App, platform statements and payslips. It never does deduction maths, never says 'you qualify', uses no bank feeds and offers no landlord verification.
first_buyer: A bartender or server paid largely in cash (or a booth-renting stylist paid in cash and Venmo) whose tips aren't fully captured by a POS, in January 2027 when her first W-2 with Box 12 code TP arrives and she realises 2026's cash nights are unrecorded.
why_now: The 2025 law's tips deduction (up to $25k a year, tax years 2025-2028, phasing out above $150k MAGI) is covered by final regulations (TD 10044, April 2026) listing 70+ occupations. From tax year 2026, W-2s report qualified tips in Box 12 code TP and the occupation code in Box 14b (draft instructions). Employees must keep a daily tip record and report $20+ a month on Form 4070 by the 10th (Pub 531), which gives a monthly trigger. The 2027 filing season is the first without the 2025 transition relief.
competitors: Stride: free mileage and expense tracking for gig workers
Gridwise: imports gig platform earnings and tips plus mileage; Pro $9.99/month or $79.99/year
Everlance: mileage and expenses; Starter about $69.99-89.99/year (sources disagree)
Solo: gig earnings and mileage tracker (pricing unverified)
Keeper: bank-feed write-off finder and filing (pricing unverified); cash tips never touch a bank feed
Toast POS: prompts employees to declare cash tips at clock-out (employer's record)
TurboTax and TaxAct: take the deduction at filing; no daily log
Free tip-tracker apps and the paper Form 4070A daily record
price_and_margin: $39.99 a year, annual only, hard paywall: about $38 net on web checkout or $34 after Apple's 15%. Rebuild 2026 at $29, credited toward the annual plan. Cost to serve under $1 a year (storage, timestamps, on-device OCR). Realistic creator CAC $35-45, so year one roughly breaks even; profit depends on renewals, tip-out invites and the January rebuild.
channel: First 100: the creator pre-sale. First 1,000-1,500 by April 2027: paid #bartok and #servertok creators (about $150 a video, ending on the seal stamp), about $40k of creator spend, USBG chapters, and Sola/Phenix salon-suite member perks for booth renters. Amount-free tip-out links reach co-workers as a loop. Toast and 7shifts are the employer's tools and come later, if ever.
demand_test: Three weeks, about $2.5k: ten bartender and server creators send viewers to a $39 web pre-sale, while 30 bartenders get the close-time prompt by SMS. Go at 100+ pre-orders with CAC of $45 or less and 60%+ of worked shifts logged in week 3; under $25 CAC would justify market fit 6.
mvp_90_days: Weeks 1-3: demand test. Weeks 4-8: iOS and Android keypad log, server timestamp seal with visible amendments, close-time prompt (no geofence, no 'Always' location), Vision and ML Kit slip OCR, monthly 4070-style PDF, amount-free tip-out share links. Weeks 6-12: Rebuild 2026 importers (Venmo, Cash App, DoorDash, Uber statements, payslip photos) with evidence tiers, live by February 1, 2027.
kill_metric: In the test: under 100 pre-orders, CAC over $45, or under 60% of worked shifts logged in week 3. By April 30, 2027: under 1,000 payers or under 30% of rebuild buyers converting to the annual log.
risks: CAC near a year's revenue; creator conversion may not hold beyond the first wave
Gridwise, Stride or Keeper add a free tips field within a month; only sealed history and tip-out links create switching cost
The deduction ends after tax year 2028, and many low-income tipped workers owe little federal income tax anyway
Strays into tax advice if it ever estimates savings or decides who qualifies; no deduction maths, no occupation determination
Sealed records can show tips she didn't report to her employer; records are hers, exportable and deletable, with no employer accounts
Income-verification features for landlords could make it a consumer reporting agency under FCRA (unverified reading); cut
Tip-out invites must not expose a co-worker's income before he consents; amount-free links sent from her own Messages
Platform statement and payslip formats drift and break the rebuild importers
three_year: A pay map ('Friday close $212, Tuesday $64') that keeps workers renewing after the deduction lapses, plus a $19/month house sheet for small bars without Toast that run tip pools on paper, with each line confirmed by staff. Target 15-20k worker payers and 500 bars, about $0.7-0.9M ARR.
best_line: Taxes recruit her; the pay map keeps her.
